Florida Coastal Camping on the Forgotten Coast

By Jameson Redding
August 6, 2026
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
WhatsApp
Linkedin
    Email
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:07
Instaread

Florida coastal camping offers one of the best ways to experience the wild side of the Florida Forgotten Coast. Instead of crowded beaches and busy cities, this adventure follows the Florida Adventure Trail through remote forests, back roads, quiet campsites, and productive fishing waters.

I spent a week exploring this overlooked stretch of Florida with Jesse Laspeyre and Brooks Beatty. Along the way, we chased largemouth bass, redfish, and speckled trout while discovering why this region feels untouched compared to the rest of the state.

Why Coastal Camping Is Different on Florida's Forgotten Coast

The Florida Forgotten Coast surprised me from the moment we arrived.

Most people picture Florida as highways, resorts, and crowded waterfronts. Here, it was almost the opposite. Dirt roads replaced pavement, small fishing towns replaced tourist attractions, and miles of wilderness surrounded us.

That made Florida coastal camping feel like a true backcountry adventure.

We followed sections of the 1,100-mile Florida Adventure Trail, connecting rivers, forests, and coastal communities that many lifelong Floridians don't even know exist. Every turn seemed to reveal another hidden launch, scenic campsite, or quiet stretch of shoreline.

Learning to Roll with the Unexpected

No adventure goes exactly as planned.

Strong winds, changing tides, and blocked forestry roads forced us to adjust throughout the trip. One trail even ended with a fallen tree that had to be cleared before we could continue.

Those changing conditions didn't stop at the water's edge. We were constantly moving between pavement, gravel, forestry roads, and rough access points. Running the Nokian Tyres Outpost nAT as our all terrain tire gave us the overland tire performance we needed to keep exploring as the route changed.

Instead of getting frustrated, we embraced the unpredictability.

Having a comfortable camp setup made a huge difference. We could return each evening, relax, regroup, and head back onto the water without constantly packing and moving camp. That flexibility is one of the biggest advantages of Florida coastal camping, especially when weather changes quickly.

Where the Adventure Really Came Alive

Fishing was the reason we came, and the Florida Forgotten Coast delivered.

The trip started on the Wacissa River, where Jesse landed his personal best largemouth bass before I connected with a big fish on a Z-Man GOAT ToadZ. Watching each other catch fish made the day even better.

Later, we transitioned from freshwater to the saltwater flats.

Despite strong winds and dirty water, we found success targeting oyster mounds, grass edges, and deeper pockets. Those areas consistently held speckled trout and redfish as the tides moved.

One of my favorite moments came near the end of the trip. After losing what was probably the biggest redfish I'd ever seen, I stayed patient, kept casting along the shoreline, and finally landed a beautiful redfish to finish the adventure.

Is Florida Coastal Camping Worth It?

Absolutely—if you enjoy exploring beyond the typical tourist destinations.

The combination of remote camping, scenic back roads, excellent kayak fishing, and untouched coastline creates an experience that's difficult to find elsewhere in Florida.

The Florida Forgotten Coast isn't about luxury resorts or busy marinas. It's about slowing down, adapting to nature, and enjoying places that still feel wild.

If you're looking for an outdoor adventure with fewer crowds and plenty of opportunities to fish, paddle, and explore, Florida coastal camping deserves a spot on your bucket list.

There's something incredibly rewarding about following forgotten roads to forgotten waters. For me, that's exactly what made this trip unforgettable.

FAQs

What is Florida coastal camping?

Florida coastal camping combines camping near Florida's shoreline with activities like kayaking, fishing, paddling, and exploring nearby coastal ecosystems.

Where is the Florida Forgotten Coast?

The Florida Forgotten Coast stretches along Florida's Big Bend region and includes quiet coastal towns, wildlife areas, forests, and sections of the Florida Adventure Trail.

Is the Florida Forgotten Coast good for kayak fishing?

Yes. The area offers excellent opportunities to target largemouth bass, redfish, and speckled trout in rivers, marshes, oyster beds, and shallow flats.

What makes Florida coastal camping unique?

Unlike many popular Florida destinations, the Florida Forgotten Coast offers remote campsites, fewer crowds, scenic back roads, and a true wilderness experience.

What type of tire is best for the Florida Adventure Trail?

An all terrain tire makes sense for the Florida Adventure Trail because the route can take you from pavement to gravel and remote forestry roads. We ran the Nokian Tyres Outpost nAT on this trip, giving us the overland tire performance we needed for the changing road conditions we encountered.

When is the best time to visit the Florida Forgotten Coast?

We explored the Florida Forgotten Coast in April. Conditions changed throughout the trip, with strong winds, changing tides, and calmer mornings all affecting our plans. Whatever time you visit, building flexibility into your itinerary is key.

This trip reminded me just how much a good camp setup can improve an adventure. If you want to see exactly how I rigged my truck and camper for trips like this, check out my complete Four Wheel Camper Project M build.
